question.leadin: One noblewoman from this family was blamed for instigating a massacre of thousands of Huguenots in France on St. Bartholomew's Day.
question.text: Name this European family to which Catherine, the wife of King Henry II, belonged. Cosimo established this family's dominance over the city of Florence during the Renaissance.
question.answerHtml: Medici [MEH-dih-chee] family (accept Catherine de’ Medici or Cosimo de’ Medici )
question.clue: People with this last name founded a Platonic Academy and were targeted in the Pazzi Conspiracy.

swap.leadin: This leader and his mistress Claretta Petacci were allegedly hung on meathooks.
swap.text: Name this former Socialist and fascist world leader. He was nicknamed "Il Duce" (eel doo-chay) and was supported by the paramilitary Blackshirts.
swap.clue: This leader used claims of native irredentism to force King Zog into exile and justify his country's occupation of Albania.

question.leadin: In 415 BCE, an expedition of over 100 triremes [tri-reems] sailed to this island to attack the city of Syracuse.
question.text: Name this island off the coast of Italy.
question.clue: Alcibiades led a disastrous expedition to capture this region.

swap.text: Martin Waldseemuller named America after this man who explored the Brazilian territory.
swap.clue: In the Mundus Novus, this man informed Lorenzo de Medici that the land that he discovered was not Asia, but a new landmass.

question.leadin: The Black Death may have first arrived in Europe during the Golden Horde's siege of this city's colony of Caffa.
question.text: Name this Italian city. This maritime republic was the home city of Christopher Columbus.
question.clue: This city was led for much of its history by the Boccanegra family and was the home of admiral Andrea Doria.

swap.text: This massive Italian ship collided in 1956 with the MS Stockholm just off the coast of Massachusetts, and sank eleven hours later. Almost all of the deaths came from the initial collision.
swap.clue: This man, the primary target of the Fieschi conspiracy, was depicted as the god Neptune by Agnolo Bronzino.

question.leadin: Renaissance Italy housed multiple notable city states.
question.text: This city-state's Palazzo Vecchio overlooks the Piazza della signoria. This city's Uffizi museum was once the office of the Medici family.
question.clue: This Tuscan city traditionally rivaled Pisa before conquering it in 1406.

swap.leadin: The government attempted to abate this period with the so-called "historic compromise."
swap.text: Name this period in which the Red Brigades instigated many terrorist attacks. This period climaxed with the murder of former Prime Minister Aldo Moro.
swap.clue: This period was preceded by a series of violent strikes known as the Hot Autumn.

question.leadin: Identify these left-leaning European leaders from the twentieth century.
question.text: This Italian Prime Minister's organization of the "Historic Compromise" - a coalition between his Christian Democracy party and the communists - so irked Mario Moretti that the Red Brigades kidnapped and eventually executed him in 1978.
question.clue: The trial at Turin of Renato Curcio and fourteen other accused terrorists placed him in danger.

swap.leadin: This expedition ended following the successful siege of Gaeta.
swap.text: Name this Sicilian expedition which overthrew the Bourbon king Francis II.
swap.clue: The primary opponent was Francis II, who was decisively defeated at Milazzo after failing to stop a landing at Marsala.

question.text: Though he spent much of his time in London, this Italian jounralist founded the "Young Italy" movement of which Garibaldi had once been a member, as a means of unifying Italy under a liberal democracy.
question.clue: As a triumvir of the short-lived 1849 Roman Republic, this man led the resistance against Napoleon III's invasion to restore Pius IX to power.

swap.text: This Italian revolutionary tried to kill Napoleon III in 1858 by throwing bombs at the imperial carriage. He failed and was guillotined later that year.
swap.clue: Mazzini sent this man to begin an uprising in Carrara. Lord Palmerston's first government collapsed after this man's failed assassination attempt on Napoleon III.

question.leadin: King Ferdinand IV created the title "Duke of Bronte" for Horatio Nelson after a naval blockade forced Jacobin troops in this city to surrender to Fabrizio Ruffo's Sanfedisti.
question.text: Name this city whose poorest class, the Lazzaroni, rose up against the French-backed Parthenopean Republic. The Expedition of the Thousand captured this capital of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.
question.clue: A tax on fruit prompted a fisherman to lead a rebellion in this city, in which Fabrizio Ruffio led the Papal Sanfedismo movement to overthrow the Napoleonic Parthenopean Republic.

swap.leadin: This ruler conducted currency reforms by introducing the silver coin called the grosso.
swap.text: Name this man whose lasting accomplishment was diverting a European army to sack Zadar and then Constantinople during the Fourth Crusade.
swap.clue: This leader refused rulership of the newly created Latin Empire, instead placing his fellow crusader Baldwin of Flanders on the throne.

question.text: The failure of the 'Pact of Pacification' was followed in 1922 by this event, in which, after they had taken control in the North, the fascisti marched south, forcing the resignation of Luigi Facta as Prime Minister and the appointment of Mussolini.
question.clue: This October 1922 action that led to the ouster of Luigi Facta and set the stage for the ascent of a certain right-wing European party along with the assassination of Giacamo Matteotti two years later.

swap.leadin: During this battle, the Arditi Corps earned the nickname "the Caimans of the Piave" for swimming back and forth across the frigid Piave River to carry messages.
swap.text: Name this 1918 victory for Armando Diaz, who had replaced Luigi Cadorna the previous year, which led to the Armistice of Villa Giusti.
swap.clue: This battle fought exactly one year after Caporetto, which led directly to the Armistice of Villa Giusti. This battle marked the end of World War One on the Italian front.

question.leadin: A former writer for a magazine whose name translates as "the manifesto" analogized this organization's trajectory to that of the legendary Tailor of Ulm in a 2009 book that was republished by Verso in 2011.
question.text: Name this organization, whose leaders advocated a theory known as "polycentrism." One of this organization's founders, Palmiro Togliatti ("toll-YAH-tee"), names a city that was the headquarters of VAZ.
question.answerHtml: Italian Communist Party [or PCI; or Partito Comunista Italiano; prompt on Communist Party or Partito Comunista] (The magazine is titled Il Manifesto. The city is Tolyatti, Russia.)
question.clue: This organization joined the CLN on the eve of World War II as part of a strategy known as the Salerno turn.

swap.text: The essay highlights the non-participation of Elisabetta, a duchess of this family, in activities in The Book of the Courtier over which she ostensibly presides. Isabella D'Este married into this ruling family of Mantua.

question.text: Zeno eventually came to see Odoacer as a major rival, causing him to offer Italy to this Ostrogothic ruler, who killed Odoacer during a banquet.
question.clue: Procopius's Secret History suggests that Justinian had his daughter Amalasuntha murdered in a bathtub after she succeeded this ruler.

swap.text: This chief of staff of the Italian Army lost his position to Armando Diaz after getting his ass handed to him at Caporetto.
swap.clue: This Italian general from World War I who was dismissed after his army was shoved back at the Battle of Caporetto.
